schoolReviews.review: Registration staff is rude and condescending they do not understand that if you do not have the birth certificate you can use other documents and that if they deny a student enrollment into their school based on not having the birth certificate they are in violation of the federal law and several staff members have stated that they are not in violation the federal law they don't have to abide by it and they're all rude disrespectful I would never recommend a child go to the school even if they were desperate and this was the score the only had an available space I would not enroll a child there

My son is in his 3rd year at Charles Wright and my daughter in her 2nd year, and we have had nothing but excellent experiences with all of the teachers, and with the principal, Mrs. Slaven, and Assistant Principal, Mrs. Barber. There is also a very active Parent Teacher Club that has raised several thousand dollars over the past 3 years, money that has been used to improve the playground equipment, provide teachers with supplies and classroom tools, and most importantly, restored the ability of all classes to go on big field trips several times throughout the year! My kids and I love Charles Wright! Staying involved and getting to know the teachers, principals, and staff is key, and has allowed us to benefit from constant support and opportunities to improve. Only a handful of parents come to the PTC meetings, and attendance of school functions by families of students seems low.

My children do not like this school, this school does not have a anti bully policy in place. if your child is bullied here they just say stop it and put the children on opposite sides of the playground.DONT WORK!!My children are miserabl;e at this school, the teachers they have are rude and do not interact with parents except once a year for a quick parent / teacher conference if thats what you wanna call it.Not very many school activities for kids either, barley any fundraisers.The principle Ms. Slaven is not very helpful either!!

we will really miss having last years principle he treated all the kids with respect and cherished each one of them. he was awesome... hopefully this year will still be good with a new principle and all.

schoolReviews.review: I have 2 students here. The one senior and one freshman. I like that it is the type of school where most students know each other from their younger days and yet, they have been welcoming to students like mine, who are transplants. Parents seem to be engaged, FFA seems great and there are lots of programs, clubs and pathways for students to explore.

This is an amazing campus to work at. I feel supported by both administration and parents, which is not always the case at other schools. I have some of the best kids in the district in my classes and for the most part, they all work hard and do their best. This is a wonderful school!!!

schoolReviews.review: My two children are in the MONTESSORI PROGRAM at John Muir, and this reviews focuses specifically on that program. I have been amazed at the level of both social AND academic growth of my kids since they have entered this program. The nature of the program teaches them to be self-motivated, curious and excited about learning, and most importantly, kind and compassionate. My kids can progress at their own pace, learn an amazing amount about different cultures, and also learn a deep respect for their peers and the diversity in their community. I cannot recommend the Montessori program more highly. The program is moving to Ada Givens in the Fall of 2017.

Before my son transferred to John Muir he was cast as a problem child. When he started 4th grade at John Muir I went to talk to his teacher regarding his "behavioral problems" she could not believe that he had ever had a problem. Not only was he at the top of the class academically, she told us he was kind, helpful, respectful, and a perfect student. She was flabbergasted at how he could be seen as a problem. He continued his elementary education at John Muir and did wonderfully. My daughter now attends first grade their and we are still just as pleased. The staff is very friendly, helpful, and professional. The teachers are excellent and the homework that my kids bring home is above what is expected for the grade. I know that the state scores are low but I believe that this has to do with a lot of the students being ESL students still learning English. The district is in a low income area but the school does not reflect this at all. I am proud to be a parent of a John Muir student.

This school has wonderful and caring teachers, administrators and staff. The principal is first-rate and he gives his staff the tools to do their jobs effectively. It is one of the oldest schools in the Merced County School District but the school seems more contemporary because it is academically and technologically on the forefront such as offering Montessori classes in grades 1-3 and having iPads in some of the classrooms. The one area of improvement would be to have more field trips which is often a function of budgetary constraints. However, even trips to local museums and other sites (which is more economical) would enhance student learning and engender greater appreciation for the community.

I have four children attending John Muir. They have attended since Kinder. I have always spoke so highly of their staff, teaCher, and principle until this year. Some of the teachers there lack their position as a teacher, the principle now just has little interest for what the students need. The parents are not allowed on campus, how do we maintain teacher parent communication. I find my kids believing they have more independence now since we dont get notices of mark, failing grades, and the understanding of what our children are learning. I wish i could say more good but i being lying. The only thing i can say is all my kids are doing very well, and advancing, they have good programs of education there they just need to pull together as a team. Its crazy sometimes because they are short staff,

My son went to this school for a month and a half, K teacher he first had was great and really understood our sons educational and behavioral needs. Then he was switched classes with out no parent or student notifacation, and created enough problems to tranfer him from schools.

John Muir is an excellent school with an experienced dedicated staff and one of the best principals in the county. My son is in 2nd grade and has access to both a chess club and a science club and is challenged to do his best every week. I can recommend this school without reservations.

Wind Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wind Model, which forecasts how hurricanes and costs from resulting wind damages to structures will change over time due to climate change.

Flood Factor® is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street Flood Model, a nationwide, probabilistic flood model that shows a location’s risk of flooding from rain, rivers, tides, and storm surge. It builds off of decades of peer-reviewed research and forecasts how flood risks will change over time due to changes in the environment. Flood Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of flood.

A property's Flood Factor is an indicator of its comprehensive flood risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Flood Factors are more likely to have flooded in the past, and are more likely to flood in the future.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Flood risk accumulates over time. Cumulative risk is calculated to the largest building or center of an empty lot. Raised or elevated buildings may not be as vulnerable as ground-level buildings or buildings with basements.

Fire Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wildfire Model's nationwide, behavioral wildfire model that shows a specific location's probabilistic risk of wildfire based on the vegetation, topography, and fire weather in the surrounding area. Fire Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of fire.

A property's Fire Factor indicates its cumulative wildfire risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Fire Factors are more likely to be in a wildfire in the future.

entryPointFlyout.value:
Heat Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. Heat Factor™ uses the First Street Extreme Heat Model to determine property-specific heat risk across the United States. The model is a spatial temperature model that determines a specific location’s exposure to extreme heat events based on the surface temperature, topography, land cover, and humidity in the surrounding area.

A property's Heat Factor indicates its risk of extreme heat exposure over the next thirty years, ranging from 1 (minimal risk) to 10 (extreme risk). Heat Factors are based on the current average daily high temperature and humidity of a property’s specific location during the hottest month of the year, and considers how it’s expected to grow over the next 30 years.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on current and future temperature and humidity in the area and at this specific location, this property has severe heat risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's heat risk is increasing as weather patterns change.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows the number of days exceeding what is considered a hot day at this property. This is defined by using the 98th percentile “feels like” temperature in this area, or the hottest 7 days in the 4km area surrounding this property for a given year and using the lowest “high” temperature from those 7 days as a base. A property may have more or less hot days than the surrounding area depending on its individual exposure to heat.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: A “hot day” in this area is considered to be any day with a “feels like” temperature of 104º. Over the next 30 years, this property is expected to see a 9% increase in the number of hot days per year.
